source_admission: Published values used as constants or quoted ranges in computing.py and computing.md; no external dataset files are admitted. 'access' records how far each source was read on 9 October 2026: 'full text' means the document itself was read, at least the sections named; 'abstract' or 'page' means only that; 'via search summary' means the value was taken from a web search's summary of the source and the source itself was not opened. Copies of the documents read are kept with the domain's run records on the research drive (provisioning-runs/computing_sources), not in the repository.

sources.citation: NVIDIA, H100 Tensor Core GPU specifications (SXM)
sources.use: 989 TFLOP/s dense 16-bit (1,979 with sparsity), 67 TFLOP/s 32-bit, 34-67 TFLOP/s 64-bit, up to 700 W: about 1.4e12 FLOP per joule at 16 bits, the array study's figure

sources.citation: NVIDIA 2016, Tesla P100 PCIe datasheet
sources.use: 9.3 TFLOP/s 32-bit at 250 W: the hardware of the COSMO baseline, 2.6 times less efficient at 32 bits than the H100

sources.citation: NVIDIA 2020, A100 80GB Tensor Core GPU datasheet
sources.use: 19.5 TFLOP/s 32-bit at 400 W (SXM4): the hardware of the minimal-cell simulation, 2.0 times less efficient at 32 bits than the H100

sources.citation: NVIDIA 2024, DGX H100 datasheet
sources.use: 130.45 kg for 10.2 kW: 12.8 kg of server per kW, the high end of processor mass

sources.citation: Ho, Erdil & Besiroglu 2023, Limits to the energy efficiency of CMOS microprocessors, IEEE International Conference on Rebooting Computing; arXiv 2312.08595
sources.use: maximum CMOS efficiency 4.7e15 FLOP/J at 4 bits (geometric mean, 0.7 orders of magnitude spread), 2.9e14 at 16 bits, about 207 times the H100; 30-3,000 transistor switches per 4-bit operation; energy quadratic in precision; efficiency doubling every 1.57 years to 2000 and 2.7 years after; a GPU's useful life about 5 years; irreversible logic only

sources.citation: Landauer 1961, Irreversibility and heat generation in the computing process, IBM Journal of Research and Development 5, 183
sources.use: erasing a bit dissipates at least kT ln 2
sources.access: not re-read here; the principle as stated in Lloyd 2000, Ho et al. 2023 and Frank et al. 2020, read in full

sources.citation: Bérut, Arakelyan, Petrosyan, Ciliberto, Dillenschneider & Lutz 2012, Experimental verification of Landauer's principle linking information and thermodynamics, Nature 483, 187
sources.use: the heat of erasing a one-particle memory approaches Landauer's bound in slow cycles

sources.citation: Bennett 1973, Logical reversibility of computation, IBM Journal of Research and Development 17, 525
sources.use: computing can be made logically reversible at every step, dissipating much less than kT per step

sources.citation: Frank, Brocato, Conte, Hsia, Jain, Missert, Shukla & Tierney 2020, Exploring the ultimate limits of adiabatic circuits, Sandia report SAND2020-8419C
sources.use: fully adiabatic CMOS can cut switching losses by orders of magnitude and dissipate below kT ln 2 per operation when logically reversible; cooling from 4 K costs about 400 times the heat removed

sources.citation: Lloyd 2000, Ultimate physical limits to computation, Nature 406, 1047; arXiv quant-ph/9908043
sources.use: a 1 kg, 1 litre computer performs at most 5.4258e50 operations/s on about 2.13e31 bits; ordinary matter computing with its nuclear spins about 1e40 operations/s per kg

sources.citation: Lloyd 2002, Computational capacity of the universe, Physical Review Letters 88, 237901; arXiv quant-ph/0110141
sources.use: the universe can have performed no more than 1e120 operations on 1e90 bits

sources.citation: Margolus & Levitin 1998, The maximum speed of dynamical evolution, Physica D 120, 188
sources.use: a system of mean energy E passes through at most 2E/(pi hbar) orthogonal states a second, the bound behind Lloyd's limit
sources.access: abstract via search summary; the bound as used in Lloyd 2000

sources.citation: Bremermann 1962, Optimization through evolution and recombination, in Self-Organizing Systems (Yovits, Jacobi & Goldstein, eds.), Spartan Books
sources.use: c^2/h, about 1.36e50 bits/s per kg, recomputed from the shared constants

sources.citation: Sandberg & Bostrom 2008, Whole brain emulation: a roadmap, Future of Humanity Institute technical report 2008-3
sources.use: processing per emulation level (Table 9): 1e15 FLOPS for an analog population model, 1e18 spiking network, 1e22 electrophysiology, 1e25 metabolome, 1e26 proteome, 1e27 states of protein complexes, 1e30 distribution of complexes, 1e43 single molecules at 1e3 FLOPS per molecule and 1e15 steps/s; the workshop's consensus at levels 4-6; storage per level (Table 8)
sources.access: full text (Tables 8 and 9 and the section on levels read)

sources.citation: Carlsmith 2020, How much computational power does it take to match the human brain?, Open Philanthropy
sources.use: more likely than not that 1e15 FLOP/s is enough to perform tasks as well as the human brain, under 10% that more than 1e21 is needed; mechanistic method 1e13-1e17; the brain's 20 W allows at most about 7e21 bit erasures a second
sources.access: summary post (EA Forum, Open Philanthropy) read; the report was unreachable and not read

sources.citation: Bostrom 2003, Are you living in a computer simulation?, Philosophical Quarterly 53, 243
sources.use: a human brain at about 1e14 or 1e16-1e17 operations/s; the mental history of humankind, 100 billion people of 50 years, at 1e33-1e36 operations; a planetary-mass computer at 1e42 operations/s; Drexler's sugar-cube computer at 1e21 instructions/s

sources.citation: Bradbury 1999, Matrioshka Brains, working manuscript (not peer reviewed)
sources.use: a single-layer Matrioshka brain on 1e26 W at 1e42 operations/s, a multi-layer one on 3e26 W at 3e42, from rod logic at 1e-16 J per operation (Table 5, Table 1); nested shells replace earlier planet-sized Jupiter brains, which could not shed a star's power without melting and would spend much of their energy circulating coolant (footnote 1)
sources.access: full text (Tables 1 and 5 and footnote 1 read)

sources.citation: Cotra 2020, Forecasting TAI with biological anchors, Open Philanthropy draft report, as summarised by Ho 2022, Grokking 'Forecasting TAI with biological anchors', Epoch AI
sources.use: the evolution anchor, the computation of all nervous systems through evolution, about 1e41 FLOP; the lifetime anchor about 1e28 and the neural-network anchors 1e32-1e37 FLOP
sources.access: Ho's summary read; Cotra's report not read

sources.citation: Hanson 2016, The Age of Em: Work, Love and Life when Robots Rule the Earth, Oxford University Press
sources.use: trillions of brain emulations, typically about 1,000 times human speed

sources.citation: Schulthess, Bauer, Wedi, Fuhrer, Hoefler & Schär 2019, Reflecting on the goal and baseline for exascale computing: a roadmap based on weather and climate simulations, Computing in Science & Engineering 21(1), 30
sources.use: the goal of global 1 km simulation with 180 levels to 100 km at one simulated year a day; COSMO near-global at 0.93 km, 60 levels and 6 s steps ran 0.043 simulated years a day on 4,888 P100 nodes at 596 MWh per simulated year; shortfalls of 101-247 times, coupling 1.2 of them; 100 m resolution a factor of 1e5 or more beyond today's simulations
